title: Natural Domain and Range of a Rational Difference of Squares
originalTopic: Functions and Graphs: Natural Domain and Range
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Find the natural domain and range of the real-valued function G(t) = \frac{2}{t^2 - 16}.

steps.title: Identify Denominator Singularities
steps.explanation: The denominator cannot equal zero, which occurs when t^2 = 16, or t = 4 and t = -4.
steps.why: A rational expression is undefined at the roots of its denominator.

steps.title: State the Natural Domain
steps.explanation: Excluding the two vertical asymptote locations t = -4 and t = 4 leaves the union of three disjoint open intervals.
steps.why: The real line punctured at two isolated points splits into three open components.

steps.title: Analyze Range for Exterior Inputs
steps.explanation: When |t| > 4, the denominator t^2 - 16 is strictly positive. As |t| approaches 4 from the outside, G(t) grows arbitrarily large toward positive infinity. As |t| approaches infinity, G(t) decays toward 0 from above, covering (0, inf).
steps.why: Continuous positive rational functions approaching vertical and horizontal asymptotes cover all values in (0, inf).

steps.title: Analyze Range for Interior Inputs
steps.explanation: When |t| < 4, the denominator is negative, taking values in [-16, 0). At t = 0, G(0) = 2/(-16) = -1/8, which is the maximum output on this interval. As |t| approaches 4 from inside, G(t) approaches negative infinity, covering (-inf, -1/8].
steps.why: The denominator achieves its most negative value at t = 0, bounding the negative branch from above at y = -1/8.

steps.title: Combine the Range Components
steps.explanation: Combining the output sets from both exterior and interior inputs produces the complete range: (-inf, -1/8] U (0, inf).
steps.why: The range of a function is the union of the images of all connected components of its domain.
